title: OKR → Initiative Ownership Lifecycle and Decision-Rights Matrix
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a lightweight, operational playbook that maps company-level OKRs to owned initiatives, defines the lifecycle stages for initiative ownership, and codifies decision rights across functions.

Scope: company-level OKRs (top 8), associated initiatives spanning Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM. Deliverables include a spreadsheet matrix, a short playbook doc, and templates for Quarterly Initiative Hand-offs (ownership transfer, escalation path, success metrics). Excludes team-level OKR templates — follow-on work.

Why this matters: We repeatedly see drift between an OKR owner (exec or PM) and initiative leads during rollouts — causing duplicated work, unclear escalation, and late detection of blockers. A clear lifecycle + decision-rights matrix will reduce meeting overhead, speed escalations, and make quarterly rollouts measurable.

Success criteria:
- Matrix published and adopted by >80% of initiative leads for the upcoming quarter.
- Playbook reduces cross-team triage meetings by 25% (tracked via meeting calendar samples).
- 90% of initiative owners use the Quarterly Initiative Hand-off template before dev kickoff.

acceptance_criteria: Matrix maps each company OKR to at least one initiative and lists primary owner, secondary owner, and escalation contact.
Lifecycle stages are defined with entry/exit criteria and a template for required artifacts at each stage (PRD link, rollout checklist, SLOs).
Decision-rights table clarifies who can approve scope changes, resource reallocation, and go/no-go for rollouts.
Quarterly Initiative Hand-off template is used by at least 80% of initiative leads in the first rollout.
